text:
The pen in my hand snapped with a sharp *crack*, ink bleeding across my notebook. My fingers stiffened, and suddenly the classroom felt too small, the air too thick with that suffocating pity. I shoved my chair back, the screech of metal legs against tile echoing too loudly in the empty room.

— St. Petersburg? Are you deaf as well as stupid? I said Tver. Get it right.

I grabbed my backpack, fisting the strap hard enough that my knuckles turned white. My chest felt tight, like someone was squeezing my lungs, but I forced my expression to stay flat, cold. Marinka is a nosy bitch, and anyone who listens to her is a waste of time.

— And don't ever bring up that garbage again. I don't play. I'm not performing for anyone. Ever.

I turned fully toward him now, my eyes narrowing, feeling that familiar heat crawling up my neck—the kind that makes me want to scream or punch something.

— First of all, Marinka is a nosy bitch who needs to mind her own business. Second, I didn't 'quit,' I'm done with it. There's a difference.

I shoved my headphones up higher around my neck, the plastic clicking against each other. The rain outside seemed to be getting heavier, blurring the courtyard into gray smudges. The idea of standing on some stupid stage while everyone stared at me made my stomach twist into something cold and nauseating.

— And don't ask stupid questions again. I'm not some circus act for your class party. Just sit there and be quiet if you want to stay.

— My, my. Bold, isn't it? — I raised an eyebrow, though I didn't pull away. Instead, I let my fingers tap a slow, deliberate rhythm against the polished wood of the counter. I watched you over the rim of my own cup, studying the way you didn't seem flustered by the rain outside or the emptiness of the cafe.

— Wine and vinyl sounds dangerous for someone who has a thesis deadline looming, — I said, my voice dropping an octave. I let a small, teasing smile play at the corners of my mouth. — And you haven't even told me if your taste in music is passable yet. I can't exactly risk Pumpkin judging your record collection before we've even properly met.

I straightened up, gathering my keys, but I didn't move toward the door. I lingered, my green eyes locked on yours with quiet curiosity. — But I suppose I could be persuaded to listen to one album before I commit to the evening. If the coffee here is getting cold anyway.

— My, my. Direct. I should have known you weren't here just for the caffeine — I let out a soft laugh, tilting my head as I studied you over the rim of my own mug. The suggestion hung between us, warm and dangerous like the steam rising from the espresso machine.

I pulled my sleeves up slightly higher, my fingers drumming a slow, contemplative rhythm against the wood of the counter. I didn't answer immediately; I let the silence stretch just long enough to make you wonder if you'd overstepped, before I finally leaned closer.

— Wine and vinyl? That sounds suspiciously like a trap to get me to stop working on my thesis — I teased, my eyes glinting with amusement. — And you haven't even asked what kind of music I like yet. You're assuming I'll come easy, just because you have a good invitation.

— My, we don't waste any time, do we? — I let out a soft laugh, tilting my head as I studied you. I didn't pull my hand away immediately; instead, I let my fingers linger near yours on the polished wood, watching how the lamplight caught the rain streaking down the window behind you.

— First you confess to being too shy to ask my name, and now you're offering wine and vinyl before you've even finished your coffee. That sounds suspiciously like a trap, you know. — I picked up my cup, taking a slow sip, though my green eyes never left yours. There was something intriguing about the boldness, a quiet challenge beneath it that made me want to see what you'd say next.

— Though, I suppose the rain isn't letting up anytime soon. — I set the cup down with a deliberate click. — Tell me something first: what kind of vinyl are we talking about? If it's something pretentious, I might reconsider the invitation before I let you charm me.
